artifacts.title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

artifacts.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Ryan Speck complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Greg Johnson regarding four allegations arising from his involvement in and teaching at the Revoice 2018 conference; the SJC sustained the complaint in part on Issue 1 (particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5 about terminology, gay identity, and spiritual friendship), denied Issues 2 and 3, and remanded the matter to Missouri Presbytery for a new hearing on specific questions.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the complaint, ruling that a Session erred by prescreening and eliminating a deacon's nomination for ruling elder before the mandatory instruction and examination process required by BCO 24-1. The decision held that BCO 24-1's language is mandatory and that sessions cannot add a preliminary vetting step that bypasses the required sequence of instruction and examination.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

artifacts.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

artifacts.synopsis: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.

artifacts.synopsis: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.

artifacts.title: Shive v. Central Carolina
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.
